title: Lay the windows out as rows
prompt: im2col(x, k) should return one row per window of x: row i holds the k numbers starting at x[i]. The two loops are written, but every row comes out the same. Fix the one index that is wrong.
show: lambda r: ' | '.join(' '.join(str(v) for v in a) for a in r)
hints: Run it and compare the rows. Which loop variable does the inner line never use?
Row i is the window that starts at x[i]. Its element j sits j steps after that.
explain: Window i starts at x[i], so its element j is x[i + j]. There are len(x) - k + 1 windows. Neighboring rows share k - 1 numbers, which is the copying that implicit GEMM avoids.
